GSPip

An R package for marker quality control, construction of genomic relationship matrices (GRMs) with optional marker weights, STPGA training-population optimization, and GBLUP evaluation with or without genotype-by-environment effects.

The programmatic package API provides build_grm(), optimize_training_population(), run_gblup_single(), and run_gblup_gxe(). Editable thin-wrapper workflows are installed as templates and can be located or copied with gspip_script().

The scripts are designed to fail early on invalid settings or inputs. They check identifiers, matrix dimensions and positive definiteness, finite trait values and weights, fold settings, output collisions, and the conditions needed by each model. Existing outputs are never replaced unless overwrite_outputs <- TRUE.

Order Script Purpose
1 grm_builder.R Marker QC, optional imputation, equal- or supplied-marker-weight GRM, optional clusters
2 optimize_training_population.R Select a fixed-size training set with STPGA and compare it with equal-size random sets
3a gblup_cv_single.R Repeated CV or fixed training/target evaluation with one BLUE per genotype
3b gblup_cv_gxe.R Repeated CV or fixed training/target evaluation with one BLUE per genotype x environment

To run a script, edit the SETTINGS section at the top, then run the whole script. Every output file name starts with the run_label setting.

Installation and quick start

Install the development version from GitHub:

install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("FAkohoue/GSPip")

Install from the local checkout during development:

install.packages("D:/OneDrive - CGIAR/GitHub libraries/GSPip",
                 repos = NULL, type = "source")

Build a GRM directly from R:

library(GSPip)

result <- build_grm(
  geno_file = "path/to/genotypes.csv",
  output_dir = "path/to/results",
  input_format = "auto",
  run_label = "trial1",
  imputation_method = "none"
)
print(result)

Optimize a training population programmatically with optimize_training_population(), or copy an editable workflow template:

Copy an editable workflow template:

gspip_script("optimize_training_population", copy_to = "analysis/")
gspip_script("gblup_cv_single", copy_to = "analysis/")

ASReml-R is required only when run_gblup_single(), run_gblup_gxe(), or their editable wrappers are executed. It still needs a separate VSNi installation and valid license. Use a new run_label for each analysis; the workflows stop before replacing existing results unless explicitly allowed.

Paths may be absolute or relative to the R working directory. For a reproducible shared analysis, prefer project-relative paths and record the commit hash used for the run.

Complete example data

GSPip ships a complete, mutually aligned example set with 120 genotypes, 240 markers, three populations, and three environments. Load every R-native object as one list:

data(gs_example_all)
names(gs_example_all)
dim(gs_example_all$geno) # 120 x 240
dim(gs_example_all$grm)  # 120 x 120

Individual datasets are also available through data(), including gs_example_geno, gs_example_marker_map, gs_example_marker_weights, gs_example_blues_single, gs_example_blues_gxe, gs_example_candidate_ids, gs_example_target_ids, gs_example_grm, and gs_example_truth.

Equivalent numeric, HapMap, and VCF genotype files and all workflow inputs are installed under extdata:

numeric_file <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example_genotypes_numeric.csv", package = "GSPip"
)
grm_file <- system.file("extdata", "example_grm.csv", package = "GSPip")
single_blues <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example_BLUEs_single.csv", package = "GSPip"
)
gxe_blues <- system.file(
  "extdata", "example_BLUEs_gxe.csv", package = "GSPip"
)

The set also includes external marker weights, candidate and target ID tables, simulation truth, and example_manifest.csv, which maps every file to its purpose. Regenerate all packaged data from the repository root with:

source("data-raw/generate_example_data.R")

The generator uses base R, protects existing outputs by default, and accepts GS_EXAMPLE_OVERWRITE=true for deliberate non-interactive regeneration.

[!IMPORTANT] Check for a weight or SE column before running cross-validation. The two CV scripts do not behave the same way when both columns are absent. Do not create an artificial Weight = 1 column while keeping fix_stage1_error <- TRUE; that would force the residual variance to 1 rather than estimate it from the data.

If the data has no Weight or SE column

Script Can it run without Weight and SE? Required action
gblup_cv_single.R Yes Set weight_col <- NULL, fix_stage1_error <- FALSE, and nonmarker_effects <- FALSE
gblup_cv_gxe.R No Supply a valid weight column or SE column. The script stops before model fitting if both are absent

For the single-genotype script, the no-weight configuration is:

weight_col        <- NULL
fix_stage1_error  <- FALSE
nonmarker_effects <- FALSE

This gives every observed BLUE equal weight and lets ASReml estimate the residual variance. The se_col setting is ignored. The non-marker effect must be disabled because, with one record per genotype and an estimated residual scale, it cannot be separated from the residual.

For the G × E script, at least one real precision measure is required:

  • If the weight column exists, its positive finite values are used.
  • If a weight is missing but the SE is available, the script uses 1 / SE^2 for that row.
  • The entire weight column may be absent when the SE column is present, and vice versa.
  • A row without a trait value needs neither a weight nor an SE because it does not contribute to model fitting or metrics.
  • If an observed row has neither a valid weight nor a valid SE, the script stops and identifies the problem before fitting any model.

If the data has no Population or stratum column

Both CV scripts support three explicit choices. Do not leave strata_col <- "Population" when that column is absent—the input check will stop and identify the missing column.

Choice 1: run without stratification 

strata_col             <- NULL
derive_strata_from_grm <- FALSE

In gblup_cv_single.R and G × E CV1, genotypes are allocated across folds without population balancing. In G × E CV2, rows remain balanced within environments, but not within populations. Population-specific PA_CV_within_* metrics are not produced.

Choice 2: derive genomic strata from the GRM 

strata_col              <- NULL
derive_strata_from_grm  <- TRUE
grm_strata_n_clusters   <- NULL # Automatically select k
grm_strata_max_clusters <- 10   # Evaluate k = 2, ..., 10 when the data size allows
grm_strata_n_pcs        <- 2    # May be increased, for example to 5 or 10
grm_strata_seed         <- 123

The user does not need to know the number of clusters in advance. With grm_strata_n_clusters <- NULL, the script:

  1. Calculates the requested number of leading PCs from the full GRM.
  2. Fits k-means solutions for each candidate from 2 through grm_strata_max_clusters, subject to the number of genotypes and distinct PC positions.
  3. Calculates the average silhouette width for every candidate solution.
  4. Selects the candidate with the largest average silhouette width.
  5. Uses the selected clusters to balance the CV folds.

Average silhouette width compares within-cluster cohesion with separation from neighboring clusters; larger values indicate a better-separated candidate partition. The method is used here to select an appropriate candidate count, not to claim a known true number of biological populations.

grm_strata_n_pcs <- 2 is only the default, not a restriction. Two PCs are easy to visualize and reduce the influence of low-variance noise, but they can miss structure expressed on later axes. Set this to a larger positive integer when the eigenvalue profile or biological knowledge supports doing so. K-means uses all requested PCs with their eigenvalue-based scale, so later, lower-variance PCs contribute less distance than leading PCs. Adding many weak PCs can dilute real separation, so compare the diagnostics rather than assuming that more PCs are always better.

The result is reproducible for fixed inputs, settings, R version, and package versions. The script writes three diagnostic files:

File Content
<run_label>_derived_strata_selection.csv Every candidate K, its average silhouette, minimum cluster size, total within-cluster sum of squares, and the selected solution
<run_label>_derived_strata.csv GenoID, every PC used (PC1 through PCn), and the selected Stratum for every genotype in the GRM
<run_label>_derived_strata_pc_variance.csv Eigenvalue, individual and cumulative variance percentage, and whether each PC was used for clustering

Inspect all three files before interpreting the CV results. If prior biological knowledge or the diagnostics justify a fixed value, set grm_strata_n_clusters to that integer; this is an explicit manual override and only that value is fitted.

After inspecting the automatic diagnostics, the selected count can also be supplied as n_clusters in grm_builder.R to generate a reusable _clusters.csv; its Population column can then be merged into the phenotype table before using Choice 3.

Method reference: P. J. Rousseeuw (1987), “Silhouettes: A graphical aid to the interpretation and validation of cluster analysis”.

[!CAUTION] GRM-derived clusters are unsupervised genomic groups, not automatically known biological populations or named ancestry groups. Automatic silhouette selection is a data-driven aid, not proof of a true population count. Because clustering uses markers but not trait values, it does not introduce phenotype leakage; however, balancing these clusters across folds evaluates prediction within the represented genomic structure. It does not evaluate prediction into a completely unseen population.

Choice 3: use a supplied column 

strata_col             <- "Population"
derive_strata_from_grm <- FALSE

The named column must exist, contain no missing or empty values, and assign each genotype to only one stratum. A supplied, scientifically justified population assignment is preferable to GRM-derived clusters when available.

strata_col and GRM derivation are mutually exclusive. If both are enabled, the script stops before reading the data and asks the user to select one source.

Training-population optimization with STPGA

optimize_training_population.R selects a requested number of candidate genotypes before phenotyping or model fitting. It uses genomic principal-component predictors derived from the GRM; no trait values are read by the optimizer. This separates training-set design from downstream assessment and avoids selecting a set because it happened to predict the same observed phenotypes well.

The optimizer has two modes:

Mode Required ID files Objective population
optimization_mode <- "targeted" Target file; candidate file optional The supplied target genotypes. This is the recommended mode when the future prediction population is already known
optimization_mode <- "no_test" Candidate file optional For each proposed training set, its complement in the candidate population is the test set

Candidate and target files are CSV files with one unique, non-empty ID per row in the column named by id_col (default GenoID). Every ID must be in the GRM. The two sets must be disjoint. With candidate_ids_file <- NULL, targeted mode uses every GRM genotype not in the target file as a candidate; no-test mode uses every GRM genotype as a candidate.

Minimal targeted configuration:

grm_file           <- "results/example_grm.csv"
candidate_ids_file <- "data/candidate_ids.csv" # Or NULL
target_ids_file    <- "data/target_ids.csv"
optimization_mode  <- "targeted"
training_size      <- 200
criterion          <- "PEVMEAN"

The available criteria are PEVMEAN, PEVMEAN2, PEVMAX, CDMEAN, CDMEAN2, and CDMAX. They are STPGA design criteria and are all minimized by the algorithm. PEV criteria summarize prediction-error variance, while CD criteria summarize coefficient-of-determination design loss. They are not the PVE variance-component metric reported by the GBLUP scripts.

PCs and genetic-algorithm replication

The default stpga_n_pcs <- NULL automatically uses enough positive-eigenvalue PCs to reach stpga_pc_variance_target, subject to stpga_max_pcs. Set stpga_n_pcs to a positive integer for a manual override. The optimizer writes the complete eigenvalue profile and indicates exactly which PCs were used.

STPGA’s search is stochastic and does not guarantee the global optimum. The script therefore runs ga_replicates independent searches, records each seed and solution, and selects the replicate with the smallest recomputed objective. It also evaluates random_replicates independently sampled training sets of exactly the same size. A selected set should not be treated as useful merely because the genetic algorithm returned it: inspect convergence, consistency among replicates, and its improvement over the random objective distribution.

Optimizer outputs

File Content
_selected_training.csv Best training set; directly accepted by both GBLUP scripts
_target_ids.csv Supplied target set in targeted mode, or the best training set’s candidate complement in no-test mode; directly accepted by both GBLUP scripts
_candidate_ids.csv Candidate population actually used
_ga_replicates.csv Seed, objective, recorded iterations, and best-replicate flag
_ga_training_sets.csv Every genotype selected in every GA replicate
_ga_convergence.csv Objective trajectory returned by each GA replicate
_random_benchmark.csv, _random_training_sets.csv Equal-size random objective values and membership
_pc_variance.csv GRM eigenvalues, variance percentages, and PCs used
_run_info.txt Design settings, best and random results, paths, and package versions

Evaluate the selected set in GBLUP

Set the following in gblup_cv_single.R or gblup_cv_gxe.R:

evaluation_mode   <- "fixed_split"
training_ids_file <- "results/STPGA_training_selected_training.csv"
target_ids_file   <- "results/STPGA_training_target_ids.csv"

Fixed-split mode performs one fit: every selected training genotype is assigned to training and every target genotype is held out together. k_folds, n_iterations, and base_seed do not define this split. The phenotype file must contain all listed IDs; training genotypes must have observed trait values. Target trait values may be present for retrospective assessment or missing for prediction only. The scripts write _split_ids.csv so the exact roles are preserved with the results.

For gblup_cv_gxe.R, fixed-split evaluation is genotype-level CV1 only: all environment records of a target genotype are held out. Set cv_scheme <- "CV1". The script deliberately stops if fixed-split mode is combined with CV2, because a genotype-level STPGA selection does not define which individual genotype-by-environment cells should be observed.

The same GRM must be used by the optimizer and the GBLUP analysis. For an honest performance comparison, define target membership without using its trait values and compare the optimized set with multiple equal-size random training sets under the same GBLUP model. Optimization improves a genomic design criterion; it does not guarantee better prediction ability for every trait or environment.

Package reference: STPGA 5.2.1 documentation. The package defines the targeted and no-test genetic algorithms, their minimized criteria, and recommends replicated searches because the genetic algorithm is not guaranteed to find a global optimum.

Script Packages
grm_builder.R data.table, AGHmatrix, ASRgenomics; rrBLUP only for rrblup_em imputation
optimize_training_population.R data.table, STPGA
CV scripts data.table, ASRgenomics, cluster, and asreml with a valid VSNi license

The repository’s GitHub Actions workflow parses every .R file and runs synthetic numeric, HapMap, and VCF reader tests on each push and pull request. This catches syntax errors and genotype-format regressions without requiring ASReml or private data. A full numerical run still requires the remaining packages, license, and representative input data.

Reproducibility and safe sharing

  • base_seed, qc_seed, cluster_seed, grm_strata_seed, ga_seed, and random_seed make fold assignment, imputation, clustering, optimization, and random benchmarks reproducible for fixed inputs and package versions.
  • Each run-info file records the settings, normalized input paths, input counts, and sessionInfo().
  • data/ and results/ are ignored by Git to reduce the risk of publishing private inputs or large generated files. Review git status before every push.
  • Cross-validation metrics can legitimately be NA when a validation subset has too few usable observations, no variation, a zero trait mean, or undefined Cullis heritability. The summary’s N_iter reports how many finite iteration-level values contributed.
  • Non-converged ASReml fits are retained and flagged by Converged = 0; review them before interpreting the summary.

Before making the repository public, add the license and citation information appropriate for your organization and confirm that your ASReml license permits the intended use. ASReml itself is not redistributed here.

Pre-release smoke test

Run this once on a small, representative copy of your real data in the same R and ASReml environment your colleagues will use:

  1. Set n_iterations <- 2, k_folds <- 2, and use a temporary run_label for repeated CV.
  2. Run the GRM script and confirm that _grm_info.txt reports an invertible matrix, a positive smallest eigenvalue, and plausible diagonal/off-diagonal means.
  3. If using optimization, first use a small training_size, ga_iterations, ga_replicates, and random_replicates. Confirm the selected IDs are candidates, are unique, and are disjoint from the targets. Then restore the production settings.
  4. Run the relevant GBLUP script and confirm that every expected output is present and Converged is 1 for every fit. For repeated CV, N_iter should be 2 for the principal metrics; fixed-split output has one iteration.
  5. Check that prediction row counts and genotype/environment IDs match the inputs. In fixed-split mode, verify _split_ids.csv against the optimizer files.
  6. Run the same script again without changing run_label; it should stop before overwriting any result.
  7. Restore the intended fold, iteration, optimizer, and run-label settings before the production run.

GRM script

Accepted genotype formats

Format handling is implemented by this project’s internal read_geno() module. It is not imported from HapBlockR and is not exported as a public package function. build_grm() and the editable GRM template therefore use one implementation rather than maintaining separate parsers.

Set input_format to "numeric", "hapmap", or "vcf". With "auto", .vcf and .vcf.gz are recognized as VCF, .hmp, .hmp.txt, .hapmap, and .hapmap.txt as HapMap; every other extension is treated as a numeric table. Set the format explicitly when a file has a nonstandard extension.

Format Required layout Internal dosage
Numeric table Markers in rows; marker_col; at least two genotype columns containing 0, 1, 2, or missing Already 0/1/2
HapMap The 11 standard HapMap columns through QCcode, followed by samples Count of the second allele in alleles; common letter, two-letter, IUPAC, and 0/1/2 calls are accepted
VCF or VCF.GZ Nine fixed VCF columns through FORMAT, followed by samples; a diploid GT field Count of ALT: 0/0 = 0, heterozygote = 1, 1/1 = 2

Only biallelic markers are used. multiallelic_action <- "remove" reports and removes unsupported records; "error" stops instead. Haploid and polyploid VCF genotypes are not silently recoded. Missing numeric calls may be NA, blank, or .; missing HapMap/VCF calls use their normal format-specific notation.

Marker IDs must be unique. If a VCF record has no ID, the script creates CHROM:POS:REF:ALT; use that generated value in an external marker-weight table.

For numeric input, every column not named by marker_col, the coordinate/allele settings, meta_cols, or marker_weight_col is treated as a genotype. List every non-genotype column. The following is a valid numeric-table example; CHR, POS, REF, and ALT are optional unless Beagle is selected.

SNP CHR POS REF ALT G001 G002 G003 G004 G005 G006 …
S1_10234 1 10234 T G 0 2 2 2 0 0 …
S1_18945 1 18945 G T 0 0 0 0 2 0 …
S1_27656 1 27656 C T 0 NA 2 2 0 2 …
S1_36367 1 36367 A C 0 0 0 2 0 0 …
S1_45078 1 45078 G T 2 2 2 2 2 2 …
S1_53789 1 53789 A T 0 0 2 2 2 2 …
S1_62500 1 62500 G T 0 0 0 0 NA 0 …
S1_71211 1 71211 T A 0 0 2 0 0 2 …
S1_79922 1 79922 A G 2 2 2 2 2 2 …
S1_88633 1 88633 A C 2 2 2 2 2 2 …

Marker weights

Leave both weight settings NULL for AGHmatrix’s equal marker weights. Numeric input may name an inline column:

marker_weight_col <- "MarkerWeight"

All three formats may instead use a separate table:

marker_weights_file      <- "marker_weights.csv"
marker_weights_id_col    <- "MarkerID"
marker_weights_value_col <- "Weight"

The external table must contain one finite, non-negative weight for every biallelic marker accepted from the genotype file before QC; extra marker IDs are ignored. The script aligns the weights by marker ID after QC and passes the retained vector unchanged to AGHmatrix::Gmatrix(weights = ...). At least one retained weight must be positive. Use weights only with grm_method <- "VanRaden"; the script stops on weights with "Su". Weight scale is not normalized. See the official AGHmatrix::Gmatrix() documentation.

QC and imputation

QC is calculated internally from observed calls, before imputation:

  1. Remove genotypes whose missing fraction exceeds qc_sweep_sample.
  2. For the remaining genotypes, calculate every marker’s call rate, ALT/second-allele frequency, MAF, and observed heterozygosity.
  3. Apply qc_call_rate, qc_maf, and qc_heterozygosity, and remove markers with no calls or no allele variation.
  4. Apply the selected imputation_method to the retained matrix.

The two CSV QC reports retain both passing and failing rows, their statistics, and a failure reason.

imputation_method What happens
"none" Missing calls remain NA. The script does not stop because calls are missing. It calls AGHmatrix::Gmatrix(..., impute.method = "none"), so AGHmatrix receives the missing calls directly.
"wright" Random 0/1/2 draws use each marker’s allele frequency and a Wright inbreeding estimate for each genotype. Reproducible with qc_seed.
"random_hwe" Random 0/1/2 draws follow Hardy-Weinberg frequencies at each marker. Reproducible with qc_seed.
"rrblup_em" rrBLUP::A.mat() performs multivariate EM imputation. It can return fractional dosages and is therefore limited here to the additive VanRaden GRM.
"beagle" The retained data are written to a temporary VCF, Beagle is run through Java, and the imputed calls at the original markers are read back.

none means no imputation by this script or by the Gmatrix() argument; it does not mean that the script rejects NA. Check _grm_info.txt to see exactly how many calls were passed to AGHmatrix.

Beagle requirements and safeguards

Beagle is an external Java program, not an R package. Download its JAR separately, install Java, and set beagle_jar. Beagle imputation is LD- and position-aware, so every retained marker must have a real chromosome, positive integer position, REF allele, and one ALT allele:

  • VCF already supplies these fields.
  • Standard HapMap supplies chromosome, position, and the two alleles.
  • Numeric input must provide the columns named by chrom_col, position_col, ref_col, and alt_col.

The script refuses to invent coordinates or alleles. It accepts numeric, HapMap, and VCF input because each is converted to the same temporary VCF after QC; users do not need to convert the file manually. Configure memory and threads with beagle_memory and beagle_threads. Optional beagle_ref, beagle_map, and beagle_ne are passed to Beagle. With no map, Beagle assumes 1 cM per Mb. Its default effective population size was designed for a large outbred population and may be inappropriate for a breeding population, so set beagle_ne from defensible population knowledge. If a reference panel introduces additional variants, this script deliberately keeps only the original post-QC markers for the GRM. The command and Beagle output are saved in _beagle.log. See the official Beagle page and Beagle 5.5 documentation.

Remaining GRM steps

  1. AGHmatrix::Gmatrix() computes the "VanRaden" additive or "Su" dominance GRM. Its imputation argument is always explicitly "none", because any requested imputation has already occurred.
  2. G.inverse() tests the GRM. If necessary, the script tries G.tuneup(blend = TRUE), then G.tuneup(bend = TRUE) on the originally computed GRM.
  3. If n_clusters is set, k-means uses the first cluster_n_pcs GRM PCs. cluster_n_pcs may be greater than two. Because the number of clusters is unknown until the clustering decision is made, cluster generation is optional and downstream scripts can instead derive populations from the GRM when configured to do so.

Outputs

File Content
_grm.csv The GRM: first column GenoID, then one column per genotype
_clusters.csv Only if n_clusters is set: GenoID, every PC used (PC1 through PCn), and Population
_marker_weights_used.csv Only when weights are supplied: post-QC marker IDs and exact weights passed to Gmatrix()
_sample_qc.csv Missingness, keep flag, and failure reason for every genotype
_marker_qc.csv Call rate, allele frequency, MAF, heterozygosity, polymorphism, keep flag, and failure reason; unsupported/multiallelic IDs are also listed
_marker_map.csv Post-QC marker IDs, chromosome, position, REF, and ALT
_qc_report.txt Concise counts and thresholds
_imputed_genotypes.csv Optional final marker-by-genotype matrix when write_imputed_genotypes <- TRUE
_beagle.log Beagle command and log when Beagle actually runs
_grm_info.txt Input format, imputation and NA counts, G.inverse() checks, tune-up, diagnostics, and sessionInfo()

A marker set chosen using the trait, for example from GWAS results on the same genotypes, carries phenotype information into the GRM, even without marker weights.

Cross-validation scripts

Inputs

  • The GRM from grm_builder.R, or a compatible GRM from another source.
  • A table of stage-1 BLUEs, with BLUE weights passed to asreml(weights = ):
    • The weight column (weight_col), for example Smith weights, is used where it has a value.
    • Where it has none, the weight is 1/SE^2, from the SE column (se_col).
    • A row with a trait value but neither a weight nor an SE stops the run.
  • Rows with no trait value are kept and predicted. They do not contribute to the fit or to the metrics.
  • gblup_cv_single.R only: weight_col <- NULL means no BLUE weights, and the SE column is ignored. This also needs fix_stage1_error <- FALSE and nonmarker_effects <- FALSE. The residual variance is then estimated, so the analysis no longer treats the stage-1 errors as known.
  • gblup_cv_gxe.R does not support a no-weight analysis. It requires a weight or SE for every row with an observed trait value.
  • Every genotype in the BLUE table must be in the GRM. Genotypes in the GRM with no row in the BLUE table are allowed, and get NA in the prediction tables.

Example for gblup_cv_single.R, one row per genotype:

GenoID NBL Population SE Weight
G001 10.66 1 0.566 3.122
G002 10.92 1 0.385 6.747
G003 10.38 2 0.457 4.788
G004 8.96 1 0.461 NA
G005 9.49 2 0.449 4.960
G006 8.18 2 0.483 4.287
G007 11.18 1 0.499 4.016
G008 NA 2 NA NA
G009 8.41 1 0.417 5.751
G010 9.90 2 0.528 3.587
  • G004 has no weight, so its weight is 1/0.461² = 4.705.
  • G008 has no trait value, so it needs no weight or SE. It is predicted, but not used in the fit or the metrics.
  • Population is only needed if strata_col is set. A file with SE only, or Weight only, also works.

Example for gblup_cv_gxe.R, one row per genotype x environment:

GenoID Env NBL Population SE Weight
G001 E1 10.02 1 0.400 6.250
G001 E2 11.68 1 0.459 4.747
G002 E1 11.01 1 0.448 4.982
G002 E2 10.27 1 0.363 7.589
G003 E1 9.19 2 0.584 2.932
G003 E2 NA 2 NA NA
G004 E1 8.37 1 0.422 5.615
G004 E2 11.97 1 0.568 3.100
G005 E1 10.12 2 0.346 NA
G005 E2 10.81 2 0.304 10.821
  • Each genotype keeps the same Population in every environment.
  • G003 in E2 has no trait value: it is predicted, but not used in the fit or the metrics.
  • G005 in E1 has no weight, so its weight is 1/0.346² = 8.353.

Models

Script Model
gblup_cv_single.R y = mu + g + r + e
gblup_cv_gxe.R y = mu + E + g + r + gE + rE + e, with environment E fixed
Term Distribution Included
g, genomic N(0, G Vg) Always
gE, genomic G x E N(0, I_E ⊗ G Vge) G x E script
r, non-marker genotype effect N(0, I Vr) If nonmarker_effects <- TRUE
rE, non-marker G x E N(0, I Vre) G x E script, if nonmarker_effects <- TRUE
e, stage-1 error N(0, diag(1/w) s) Always

With fix_stage1_error <- TRUE, s = 1, so the stage-1 error variances are fixed at 1/w. The terms r and rE hold genetic variation the markers do not capture.

Evaluation modes

evaluation_mode <- "repeated_cv" uses the fold design below. evaluation_mode <- "fixed_split" uses the supplied training and target files once, as described in the STPGA section. Fixed-split target predictions remain out-of-sample; training predictions are in-sample and must not be used to claim predictive performance.

Scheme Folds assigned to What is predicted Prediction
Single script Genotypes, within stratum Each genotype, once per iteration mu + g
CV1 Genotypes, within stratum Untested genotypes mu + E + g + gE
CV2 BLUEs, within environment x stratum Tested genotypes in environments where they were held out mu + E + g + r + gE

Under CV2, a genotype with no other BLUE in training is predicted as in CV1, and is counted in Untested_val_rows. Folds have no population stratification only when strata_col <- NULL and derive_strata_from_grm <- FALSE; when GRM derivation is enabled, the derived genomic clusters are used as the strata.

Outputs

File Content
_metrics.csv Metrics per iteration and fold. Fold 0 holds metrics on predictions pooled within an iteration
_summary.csv Mean and SD of each metric across iterations
_cv_predictions.csv Out-of-sample GEBV per genotype, per iteration, and their mean. Single: mu + g. G x E: mu + mean of E + g. Under CV2, averaged over the folds where a BLUE of the genotype was held out
_cv_predictions_by_env.csv G x E only: observed BLUE and out-of-sample prediction for each row
_train_predictions.csv, _train_se.csv In-sample predictions of the vm term and their SE, averaged over the folds where the genotype was in training. Not for assessing predictive performance
_intercepts.csv Intercept of each fitted model
_run_info.txt Settings, input checks and package versions
_split_ids.csv Only in fixed-split mode: every included genotype and its training or target role
_derived_strata.csv Only when derive_strata_from_grm <- TRUE: genomic PC coordinates and the cluster used for CV stratification
_derived_strata_selection.csv Only when GRM strata are derived: candidate cluster counts, silhouette diagnostics, and the selected solution
_derived_strata_pc_variance.csv Only when GRM strata are derived: the GRM eigenvalue profile and PCs used for clustering

Metrics

Metric Definition
Vg, Vge, Vr, Vre REML estimates from the training set of the fold
Residual_scale s. Equals 1 when fix_stage1_error <- TRUE
Ve s × mean(1/w): the mean stage-1 error variance. With weight_col <- NULL, the residual variance
PVE Proportion of variance from g. Single: Vg Dg / (Vg Dg + Vr + Ve). G x E: Vg Dg / ((Vg + Vge) Dg + Vr + Vre + Ve). Dg = mean(diag(G)) − mean(G)
Heritability Cullis heritability: 1 − avsed² / (2 varG), with avsed the mean SED from predict() on the vm term, and varG = Vg × (mean diagonal − mean off-diagonal of G). G x E: on a genotype-mean basis
Heritability_min Same, with the largest SED
Heritability_max Same, with the smallest SED
Heritability_SE, _min_SE, _max_SE Delta-method SE from vpredict(). Covers uncertainty in Vg only; the SED is treated as a constant
Heritability_unscaled 1 − avsed² / (2 Vg), for reference. Not used for Accuracy
GOF In-sample correlation of observed BLUEs with fitted values, including r. G x E: within environment, then averaged
PredictionAbility Correlation of observed BLUEs with out-of-sample predictions. G x E: within environment, then averaged
Accuracy PredictionAbility / √Heritability. G x E with env_h2: mean over environments of r_j / √h2_j
RMSE Root mean squared error of out-of-sample predictions
Relative_RMSE RMSE as a percentage of the absolute trait mean; NA when the mean is zero
Standardized_RMSE RMSE divided by the SD of observed BLUEs. G x E: SD after removing environment means
*_CV_allfolds The metric on predictions pooled within an iteration. Accuracy_CV_allfolds uses the mean heritability of the folds
PA_CV_env_*, Accuracy_CV_env_* G x E only: pooled, within one environment
PA_CV_within_* Pooled, within one supplied or GRM-derived stratum, when at least min_stratum_n genotypes have usable observed/out-of-sample prediction pairs
Untested_val_rows G x E only: held-out BLUEs whose genotype has no BLUE in training
Converged 1 if ASReml reported convergence, otherwise 0

Correlations and RMSE count each BLUE equally: BLUE weights are not used in them.
